name: Yellow Sapphire
physical: Linked to a warm, energized feeling
Kept nearby for a feeling of well-being
summary: Yellow Sapphire is the golden corundum of prosperity and wisdom, known as Pukhraj in Vedic tradition and linked to Jupiter, luck and generous growth.
intro: Yellow sapphire is the golden to canary yellow variety of corundum, colored by traces of iron. It has the same hardness (Mohs 9) and brilliance as blue sapphire, but the cheerful color gives it a warmer, more radiant personality. Sri Lanka has long been the leading source, with Thailand, Madagascar, and Australia adding stones in a range of yellows from pale lemon to rich honey gold. Many yellow sapphires are heated to improve the color, though natural unheated stones command higher prices. Because it is so durable and clear, yellow sapphire is a favorite for rings, especially in gold settings, and is popular in India as a traditional astrological gem.
history: In Vedic astrology, yellow sapphire is called Pukhraj and is the gem of Jupiter, the planet of wisdom, teaching, and good fortune. It is one of the nine gems, the Navaratna, and has been worn in India for many centuries to attract prosperity and blessings, especially by those seeking success in learning or marriage. In Thailand and Sri Lanka, yellow sapphire is mined and traded widely, and in the West it has often been overshadowed by blue sapphire and citrine. Some historical yellow stones were called oriental topaz, a name used before gemologists understood corundum. Today it is a respected gem in its own right.
meaning: Yellow sapphire is traditionally associated with prosperity, luck, and wisdom. Its sunny hue is linked to the Solar Plexus and Crown chakras, and in the Vedic tradition it carries the generous, expansive energy of Jupiter. People wear it hoping to attract opportunity, support their studies, and strengthen their decision making. It is also believed to support steady optimism and to help sort out a confused mind, giving a hopeful, clear approach. Many choose it for business, teaching, or any role where guidance matters. It is typically set in gold and worn on the index finger in the Indian tradition. The energy is described as bright, warm, and expansive rather than intense.
howToUse: Wear yellow sapphire as a ring, ideally in gold, for daily support of optimism and prosperity. In the Vedic custom, it is worn on the index finger, and guidance from a knowledgeable jeweler or astrologer is common. Keep a smaller piece on your desk for study or business. Hold a stone during meditation, picturing golden light at the solar plexus and crown. Pair with citrine in a prosperity grid. Place a yellow sapphire in the southeast or wealth corner of the home in feng shui. Gift it to mark an academic or business success.
care: Yellow sapphire is very durable and can be washed with warm soapy water and a soft brush. Ultrasonic cleaners are generally safe for untreated or heat-treated stones, but avoid them for fracture-filled material. Cleanse by running water, sunlight, moonlight, sound, or smoke. Sunlight is safe, though irradiated stones may fade; ask the seller. Store apart from diamonds, which can scratch it. Rings should be removed before heavy manual work.
identify: Natural yellow sapphire often shows fine silk, color zoning, and inclusions. Synthetic yellow sapphire is real corundum but very clean. Look-alikes include citrine, yellow topaz, heliodor, and yellow glass. Citrine is far softer (Mohs 7), and glass shows bubbles. Heat treatment is common and stable, but some stones are irradiated or beryllium-diffused to boost yellow, which should be disclosed. A lab report is wise for expensive stones, especially for astrological use.

faq.q: What is yellow sapphire good for?
faq.a: Yellow sapphire is traditionally associated with prosperity, wisdom, and good luck. In Vedic tradition it is the gem of Jupiter, and people wear it to support learning, business, and steady optimism.
Pukhraj is the Sanskrit and Hindi name for yellow sapphire. It is one of the nine Navaratna gems of Vedic astrology and is linked to the planet Jupiter and to blessings of knowledge and fortune.

faq.q: Is yellow sapphire the same as citrine?
faq.a: No. Yellow sapphire is corundum with a hardness of 9, while citrine is quartz with a hardness of 7. Sapphire is denser and rarer, and costs far more, though both are used for prosperity intentions.
